claims.text: The deviation is established on the platform's own recorded distances, which POL-RD-22 makes the measure: trip_record.actual_distance_km 13.2 minus trip_record.optimal_distance_km 12.0 is 1.20 km, above the 1.0 km tolerance. That takes this case out of the within-tolerance rows (c) and (e) of POL-RD-24 and puts the driver to proof that the rider was informed and agreed before he can keep the excess distance fare he now claims back.

The GPS trace does not shrink the deviation and may not be used to re-measure it: it records 11.12 km over 49 fixes, and POL-RD-22 states in terms that a sparse trace understates a route's length. The trace is used only for which route was taken and when, and it shows the vehicle on Braddell Road from 20:54:02, off the recommended CTE corridor, matching the platform's route_deviation_detected event at 20:54:05.

No in-app notice of the deviation was given. POL-RD-21 requires the driver to inform the rider by in-app chat before or at the point of deviation. This deviation was detected at 20:54:05; the chat log's only two entries are dated 20:38:52 and 20:39:12, both before the trip began at 20:40:02, and both concern the pickup point ('At Dempsey Block 8 drop off' / 'ok'). That 'ok' pre-dates the trip and cannot be the rider's acknowledgment of a deviation, which POL-RD-21 requires the chat log or a call recording to confirm.

The driver's verbal-notice case cannot be established. POL-RD-21 admits a verbal notice only 'with the trip call recording as evidence', and says a verbal notice with no recording in the record cannot be established (POL-GEN-26). No call recording is in this record: trip_record.in_app_calls is empty and there is no other audio. The rider's statement on file is a flat denial ('He never told me anything'), and a nod, if it happened, is not an acknowledgment evidenced in the chat log or a recording. Row (a) of POL-RD-24 - informed and agreed - is unreachable, and on this record the rider was not informed.

The reroute is not shown to be traffic-justified. POL-RD-23 requires a TRAFFIC_ADVISORY that intersects the recommended route and overlaps the trip window. The LTA advisory here is an ACCIDENT on the Central Expressway (CTE) towards SLE after the Braddell Road exit, with a window that does overlap the trip, but its own derived fields carry intersects_route: null and justifies_reroute: null and mark the intersection with the recommended route as 'undetermined', and nothing else in the record - no venue_id, no party statement - places it on the route. Justification being unestablished, row (d) of POL-RD-24 applies and the excess distance fare is refunded in full.

If the judge instead finds the advisory does intersect the recommended route, the money does not change. POL-RD-24(b) covers exactly this case - traffic-justified, rider not informed, deviation over 1 km - and it too refunds the excess distance fare. The only row that would leave the driver the 0.86 SGD is row (a), and row (a) needs a rider informed and agreeing, which this record does not show.

The sum in issue is the excess distance fare and it is correctly computed: deviation 1.20 km x fare_breakdown.per_km_rate_sgd 0.72 = 0.86 SGD, with no surge, which is exactly the 0.86 SGD already refunded to the rider and recovered from the driver and exactly the amount the driver now claims back. On POL-RD-24(b) or (d) that 0.86 SGD stays with the rider and the driver's claim for its return fails.

This is a case to decide on the merits, not to hold: the contested amount is 0.86 SGD, inside POL-GEN-22's below-10.00 SGD band, and neither profile carries a fraud flag (both are 0 - the only profile field POL-GEN-22 lets a party cite for this test), so no 0.95 confidence uplift applies. The route-deviation threshold is POL-RD-25's 0.80, and every artifact this case turns on is COMPLETE at weight 1.0.

claims.text: The reroute was a response to real-time traffic and is traffic-justified under POL-RD-23: the LTA advisory records an ACCIDENT on the Central Expressway (CTE) towards SLE after the Braddell Road exit, valid 20:23:22 to 21:40:02, which covers both the trip window (20:40:02-21:04:02) and the deviation event at 20:54:05; ACCIDENT is an admissible incident type under POL-RD-23's type table; and the road the advisory names is the CTE, the expressway the platform's own recommended route ran on (optimal_route_via includes 'Central Expressway (CTE)'), at the location the trip record itself names as the point of departure - the trip record's route_deviation_detected event reads 'recommended Central Expressway (CTE), vehicle took Braddell Road', i.e. the vehicle left the recommended route at the very CTE/Braddell Road point the advisory describes. The advisory's intersects_route and justifies_reroute fields are derived as null and left to the Judge; read against the trip record's own road and exit names, the advisory sits on the recommended route segment the driver avoided.

The diversion was proportionate, not a detour for the driver's benefit: the vehicle left the recommended route at 20:54:05 and rejoined it at Serangoon Garden Way / Upper Serangoon Road at 21:02:49 - 8 minutes 44 seconds - and the trip completed in 24.0 minutes against an optimal 21.8 minutes, so the driver spent barely two minutes more than the platform's own estimate and still delivered the rider to the booked drop-off. The GPS trace is complete (49 fixes, 100% coverage, no gap above 120 s) and its road labels carry the vehicle from the PIE through Braddell Road to Upper Serangoon Road and Serangoon Garden Way without any unexplained stop.

On the platform's recorded distances, which POL-RD-22 requires be used, the deviation is trip_record.actual_distance_km minus trip_record.optimal_distance_km, that is 13.2 km minus 12.0 km = 1.20 km, and that exceeds the 1.0 km tolerance fixed by POL-RD-22. The with-tolerance rows of the POL-RD-24 matrix, (c) and (e), therefore cannot be the rows that apply to this trip.

The notification element on which the matrix turns turns on a verbal notice that this record cannot carry. The trip record's own derived block reports messages_during_trip as an empty list, and the chat log's two entries both pre-date the trip start (sent 20:38:52 and 20:39:12, before the 20:40:02 trip start) and concern only the pickup point ('At Dempsey Block 8 drop off' / 'ok'). POL-RD-21 provides that a verbal notice with no trip call recording in the record cannot be established. The record therefore does not establish that the driver failed to inform the rider; it establishes that whether he informed cannot be established.

Nor is there any recording to contradict the driver: trip_record.in_app_calls is an empty list and the evidence package for this case contains no call-recording artifact of any kind, only the trip record, trace, chat log, fare breakdown, two profiles and the traffic advisory. The driver's account of a verbal warning given at the Braddell turn-off has no corroboration, and under POL-RD-21 a recording is the only means of establishing a verbal notice; that unprovable element is exactly the open question POL-GEN-26 requires be sent to a human reviewer rather than resolved against him.

POL-RD-24 requires that exactly one row apply, and none does here: rows (c) and (e) are excluded because the 1.20 km deviation exceeds the 1.0 km tolerance, and rows (a), (b) and (d) each depend on whether the rider was informed, an element this record leaves unestablished because the only possible notice was verbal and unrecorded. POL-RD-24's closing words send a case that fits no row to escalation under POL-GEN-26, and under POL-GEN-03 an escalated case issues no monetary outcome and holds the amount - the only disposition here that does not confirm a 0.86 refund on an element the record never proves.

POL-RD-25 permits an AI ruling on a route deviation only at a confidence of 0.80 or more. The decisive element - whether the rider was informed before or at the point of deviation - is carried by no artifact at all: the chat log is silent about the deviation, the in-app call list is empty, and the trace records movement, not speech. A finding against the driver on that element therefore cannot be reached at the confidence POL-RD-25 demands, and the case goes to escalation, where the amount is held pending review instead of being paid out.

The only money the matrix can move is the excess distance fare, which POL-RD-24 fixes as deviation distance times fare_breakdown.per_km_rate_sgd, without surge: 1.20 times 0.72 = 0.86 SGD, rounded to the cent. That is exactly the sum already refunded to the rider and recovered from the driver's earnings in the interim adjustment of 2026-09-10 (payment_status PARTIALLY_REFUNDED, refund_issued_sgd 0.86). Nothing larger is in issue on this trip, so 0.86 SGD is the amount an escalation must hold while the open question is reviewed.

ruling.explanation:
To both parties. This is a route-deviation case (POLICY-ROUTE-DEVIATION v7.0.0, carrying Policy v2.1). It produces no money outcome: it goes to a human reviewer, and the 0.86 SGD now refunded to the rider and recovered from the driver's earnings is held pending that review.

What is established. On the platform's recorded distances, which POL-RD-22 requires be used, the deviation is actual 13.2 km minus optimal 12.0 km = 1.20 km, above POL-RD-22's 1.0 km tolerance; the GPS trace is used only for which route was taken, not to re-measure distance. The excess distance fare is 1.20 x 0.72 = 0.86 SGD (POL-RD-24). Rows (c) and (e) of the POL-RD-24 matrix are therefore out, as both sides agree.

Traffic justification. The LTA advisory (EV-ADVIS-05017-01) is an ACCIDENT on the Central Expressway (CTE) towards SLE after the Braddell Road exit, valid 20:23:22-21:40:02, overlapping the 20:40:02-21:04:02 trip and the 20:54:05 deviation, and ACCIDENT is an admissible incident type. Read against the trip, it lies on the recommended route: the platform's recommended route ran on the CTE and the vehicle left it exactly at the CTE/Braddell Road point the advisory names. I therefore accept the driver's position that the reroute was traffic-justified under POL-RD-23, and do not accept the rider's position that the advisory's own null derived fields leave it unplaced.

What cannot be established. That leaves rows (a) and (b), which turn only on whether the driver informed the rider. POL-RD-21 requires notice by in-app chat or by a verbal warning with a trip call recording, and says in terms that a verbal notice with no recording in the record cannot be established. The chat log's two messages are dated 20:38:52 and 20:39:12 - before the 20:40:02 trip start - and concern the pickup point, not the deviation ('At Dempsey Block 8 drop off' / 'ok'); trip_record.in_app_calls is empty and there is no call recording anywhere in the record. The driver's account of a verbal warning is therefore carried by nothing the record admits, and POL-RD-21 does not make the rider's denial its test, so the denial does not decide it either. Whether the driver notified the rider is exactly the fact POL-GEN-26 names, and a case that fits no row is escalated under POL-GEN-26 (POL-RD-24's closing words).

No AI ruling is issued. POL-RD-25 allows one only at a confidence of 0.80 or more, and the record does not carry the decisive fact. POL-GEN-22's bands do not help: the contested amount is 0.86 SGD (AI-final) and both fraud_flags are 0, but neither makes an unestablished fact established. Under POL-GEN-03, ESCALATE is terminal - no amount moves either way and the 0.86 SGD is held as it stands.

For the reviewer: the open question is whether the driver gave a verbal warning at the Braddell Road turn-off before or at 20:54:05, which only a trip call recording could establish on this record.

ruling.explanation: This is the ruling on TRP-05017 of 9 September 2026. The case cannot be decided on the merits, so it goes to a human reviewer; no money moves now. Here is the reasoning, for both of you. (1) The deviation. On the platform's recorded distances, which POL-RD-22 requires be used, the trip ran 13.2 km against a recommended 12.0 km, a deviation of 1.20 km, above the 1.0 km tolerance. The GPS trace is not used to re-measure distance (it records 11.12 km, and POL-RD-22 says a sparse trace understates a route's length); it shows only which route was taken and when. Both sides' arithmetic here is accepted, and the duration figures (24.0 min against 21.8 min optimal, 8 min 44 s off the recommended route) do not change the distance measure. So the within-tolerance rows POL-RD-24(c) and (e) do not apply. (2) The traffic. The reroute was traffic-justified under POL-RD-23. The LTA advisory LTA-TI-260909-3941 records an ACCIDENT on the Central Expressway (CTE) towards SLE after the Braddell Road exit, valid 20:23:22 to 21:40:02, which covers both the trip window (20:40:02-21:04:02) and the point at which the vehicle left the recommended route (20:54:05); ACCIDENT is an admissible incident type; the CTE is the road the recommended route uses (optimal_route_via lists 'Central Expressway (CTE)'); and the Braddell Road exit named in the advisory is exactly where the vehicle left that route, so the advisory sits on the recommended route segment the driver avoided. The rider's argument that the advisory is not shown to intersect the route is rejected - the derived fields were left null precisely because the intersection was for the Judge to determine from road, direction and location, and they determine it. Row (d) of POL-RD-24 (not traffic-justified) therefore does not apply. (3) What cannot be established. Rows (a) and (b) of POL-RD-24 both turn on whether the driver informed the rider of the deviation before or at the point of deviation. POL-RD-21 permits a verbal notice only with the trip call recording as evidence, and states in terms that a verbal notice with no recording in the record cannot be established. There is no recording: the trip record's in_app_calls list is empty and the evidence contains no audio. The chat log is complete but its only two messages (20:38:52 and 20:39:12) pre-date the trip and concern the pickup point, so they are neither a notice of the deviation nor the rider's acknowledgment of one. We therefore cannot establish that the driver notified the rider, and we cannot establish that he did not; the rider's statement is a denial, and no rule lets us decide the notification point either way. Row (a) (no refund) needs the rider informed and agreeing; row (b) (refund of the excess distance fare) needs the rider not informed. Neither can be applied. (4) The outcome. POL-RD-24 requires that exactly one row apply and sends a case that fits no row to escalation, and POL-GEN-26 requires escalation where a fact a rule needs cannot be established. That is this case: the notification fact is carried by no artifact. The case is escalated and it is terminal - no refund and no payment issues now, and the 0.86 SGD already adjusted, being the excess distance fare (deviation 1.20 km x fare_breakdown.per_km_rate_sgd 0.72 = 0.86 SGD, POL-RD-24, no surge), is held pending review rather than collected from the driver or refunded to the rider. (5) Confidence and the rider's contrary argument. Confidence is 0.50, below the 0.80 that POL-RD-25 requires before the AI may rule on a route deviation. POL-GEN-22 puts a below-10.00 SGD dispute in the band the AI may decide, but POL-RD-25 adds the 0.80 bar for this category and it is not reachable on the decisive element, so the rider's request that the case simply be decided on the merits is rejected. POL-RD-25's 0.80 threshold for an AI route-deviation ruling is met (its separate 2 km limb is not applied). No clause produces a referral.

ledger.claim: The deviation is established on the platform's own recorded distances, which POL-RD-22 makes the measure: trip_record.actual_distance_km 13.2 minus trip_record.optimal_distance_km 12.0 is 1.20 km, above the 1.0 km tolerance. That takes this case out of the within-tolerance rows (c) and (e) of POL-RD-24 and puts the driver to proof that the rider was informed and agreed before he can keep the excess distance fare he now claims back.

The GPS trace does not shrink the deviation and may not be used to re-measure it: it records 11.12 km over 49 fixes, and POL-RD-22 states in terms that a sparse trace understates a route's length. The trace is used only for which route was taken and when, and it shows the vehicle on Braddell Road from 20:54:02, off the recommended CTE corridor, matching the platform's route_deviation_detected event at 20:54:05.

No in-app notice of the deviation was given. POL-RD-21 requires the driver to inform the rider by in-app chat before or at the point of deviation. This deviation was detected at 20:54:05; the chat log's only two entries are dated 20:38:52 and 20:39:12, both before the trip began at 20:40:02, and both concern the pickup point ('At Dempsey Block 8 drop off' / 'ok'). That 'ok' pre-dates the trip and cannot be the rider's acknowledgment of a deviation, which POL-RD-21 requires the chat log or a call recording to confirm.

The driver's verbal-notice case cannot be established. POL-RD-21 admits a verbal notice only 'with the trip call recording as evidence', and says a verbal notice with no recording in the record cannot be established (POL-GEN-26). No call recording is in this record: trip_record.in_app_calls is empty and there is no other audio. The rider's statement on file is a flat denial ('He never told me anything'), and a nod, if it happened, is not an acknowledgment evidenced in the chat log or a recording. Row (a) of POL-RD-24 - informed and agreed - is unreachable, and on this record the rider was not informed.

The reroute is not shown to be traffic-justified. POL-RD-23 requires a TRAFFIC_ADVISORY that intersects the recommended route and overlaps the trip window. The LTA advisory here is an ACCIDENT on the Central Expressway (CTE) towards SLE after the Braddell Road exit, with a window that does overlap the trip, but its own derived fields carry intersects_route: null and justifies_reroute: null and mark the intersection with the recommended route as 'undetermined', and nothing else in the record - no venue_id, no party statement - places it on the route. Justification being unestablished, row (d) of POL-RD-24 applies and the excess distance fare is refunded in full.

If the judge instead finds the advisory does intersect the recommended route, the money does not change. POL-RD-24(b) covers exactly this case - traffic-justified, rider not informed, deviation over 1 km - and it too refunds the excess distance fare. The only row that would leave the driver the 0.86 SGD is row (a), and row (a) needs a rider informed and agreeing, which this record does not show.

The sum in issue is the excess distance fare and it is correctly computed: deviation 1.20 km x fare_breakdown.per_km_rate_sgd 0.72 = 0.86 SGD, with no surge, which is exactly the 0.86 SGD already refunded to the rider and recovered from the driver and exactly the amount the driver now claims back. On POL-RD-24(b) or (d) that 0.86 SGD stays with the rider and the driver's claim for its return fails.

This is a case to decide on the merits, not to hold: the contested amount is 0.86 SGD, inside POL-GEN-22's below-10.00 SGD band, and neither profile carries a fraud flag (both are 0 - the only profile field POL-GEN-22 lets a party cite for this test), so no 0.95 confidence uplift applies. The route-deviation threshold is POL-RD-25's 0.80, and every artifact this case turns on is COMPLETE at weight 1.0.

The with-tolerance rows of the POL-RD-24 matrix, (c) and (e), therefore cannot be the rows that apply to this trip.

The notification element on which the matrix turns turns on a verbal notice that this record cannot carry. POL-RD-21 provides that a verbal notice with no trip call recording in the record cannot be established.
